asSun.p: Leo is the only sign the Sun rules, and Strength is Leo's Major, so with a Leo Sun the card is a portrait of the very thing your chart is organised around. The lion in the Rider-Waite picture is the sign's own animal. The woman is what the Sun adds: steady light, able to hold heat without being burnt by it. Leo is also fixed fire, which is fire that stays put, a hearth more than a spark. Put those together and you get the card's claim about you: the will at your centre is strong enough that it never has to be rough.

Day to day this shows up as a need to mean what you do. A Leo Sun can't work at half heart for long; you either put your whole self into a thing or you quietly withdraw from it. You're loyal well past the point others would leave, because fixed fire doesn't flicker. You also have a lion's pride, and you know exactly when it's been touched. The Strength pattern is what happens next: the pause where you decide whether pride gets to answer, or whether you do. Most of your character has been built in that pause.

Your gift is that your confidence is catching. The Sun doesn't pick what it shines on, and at your best you're the same: people do better work, tell better jokes and take bigger risks in your company because you so plainly expect them to be good. You can also stay warm towards someone who is being difficult, which is rarer than courage and more useful. Kids, animals and nervous people tend to settle near you. None of this costs you much. It's simply what a well-tended fire does for a room.

The shadow is pride dressed up as composure. Because you're proud of being the steady one, you can refuse to admit a thing has hurt you, then punish it slowly with a cooled-off version of yourself. A Leo Sun that goes unappreciated doesn't always roar; sometimes it sulks with great dignity. The other trap is needing to be seen being strong, so that even your gentleness turns into a show with an audience in mind. When you catch yourself performing patience, that's the lion in a costume. Better to say plainly that you're cross.

You love the way the Sun rules the fifth house of the chart: with play, romance and open delight. You court properly, remember the details, and want your person to feel chosen in front of others. What you ask in return is to be admired out loud, and you may be shy of admitting how much that matters. Say it anyway. A partner can't guess that the capable one needs applause. When hurt, your instinct is to go regal and distant; the braver move for you is letting them see the soft underside while it still stings.

At work you need something that carries your name, even if only a few people ever read it. Anonymous effort drains a Leo Sun faster than hard effort does. You lead well because people feel safe under you: you take the blame upward and hand the credit down, and you rarely need to raise your voice. Watch two things. One is taking on a struggling project out of pride and then refusing help. The other is staying too long, since fixed fire hates to quit. Ask yourself yearly whether you're still warm in this job or merely loyal.

Next time your pride is stung, in a meeting, a text, a throwaway comment, put one hand flat on your breastbone for three slow breaths before you reply. It's the gesture from the card: a calm hand on the lion. Then say one true sentence that starts with 'That landed badly for me' rather than going cold or going loud. Do it once this week with something small. You're practising the pause between pride and response, and like any muscle it only builds with repetition.

asMoon.p: The Moon has no light of its own; it shines with what the Sun lends it. In Leo it sits in the Sun's own sign, so your feeling life borrows the Sun's manner: warm, proud, fixed fire, slow to catch and slow to go out. Strength is Leo's Major, and as a Moon card the picture turns inward. The lion is the size of what you feel. The woman is how you were built to hold it, close, with bare hands. Notice she isn't muzzling the animal. She's keeping it company, and that is the emotional skill this placement is born knowing, or born needing.

Your moods are whole-body events. Joy makes you generous and a bit loud; hurt makes you go quiet and very upright. Because Leo is a fixed sign, feelings don't pass through you quickly. You can still feel a slight from years ago at close to its first heat, and the same goes for a kindness. You need a home that's warm in the literal sense: sunlight, colour, people glad to see you at the door. And you keep your dignity about pain. Often the people closest to you learn that you were struggling only after you've already dealt with it.

You make people feel safe enough to be big. Someone crying in your kitchen never gets the sense they're too much, because you've made your peace with large feelings, starting with your own. Your affection is physical and steady: the hand on a shoulder, the meal, the fierce defence of whoever's been treated unfairly. Children in particular trust a Leo Moon, since you take their dramas seriously without being alarmed by them. It's the woman on the card again, unafraid of teeth. Your calm around strong emotion gives other people permission to have some.

A Leo Moon needs to be wanted, and the shadow is how proud you are about that need. You'd rather go without comfort than ask for it and risk a lukewarm answer. So you test people instead: go quiet, wait to see who notices, keep score when they don't. Hurt pride can sit in you for a long time looking like calm. There's also a harshness you save for yourself. You forgive others their bad days and then call your own feelings childish or attention-seeking. The lion you're roughest with is the one inside your own ribs.

In love you need affection you can see and hear. Being told, being touched, being picked first: for you these are food, not vanity. A partner who is reserved may love you completely and still leave you hungry, so it's worth saying early what warmth looks like to you. You give devotion of the old-fashioned sort and you're hard to drive away. The tender spot is being laughed at or brushed aside when you've shown something soft. When that happens you retreat behind good manners. Tell them instead, the same day if you can.

Your feelings come to work with you, whatever the job description says. You do well where there's heart in the task and some visible appreciation, and you wilt in places that are cold, grudging or sarcastic, even when the pay is good. Notice how much a single thank-you lifts your whole week; that's information about what you need, not a weakness. You're a steadying presence in a tense team, the one who can sit with an upset colleague or client. Just check you aren't soothing everyone else's lions all day and carrying your own home unfed.

Once this week, ask for comfort out loud before anyone has a chance to guess. Keep it small and exact: 'I've had a rough day, can I have a hug', or 'tell me one thing I did well'. Notice the flare of pride that says you shouldn't have to ask, and let it pass through without obeying it. That flare is the lion. Asking anyway is the hand on its mane. People who love you have usually been waiting for a way in, and a plain request is a door.

asRising.p: Your rising sign is the sign that was coming up over the eastern horizon when you were born. It sets the first house, which covers the body, your bearing and how you begin things. With Leo there, the Sun becomes the ruler of your whole chart, and Leo's Major, Strength, becomes the card of your doorway. Look at how the woman on the card stands: nothing in her hands, no armour, completely at ease beside a lion. That's the posture Leo rising hands you. Fixed fire at the front door means people meet a steady glow first, well before they meet your history or your doubts.

It's in the body before it's in anything you say. Leo rising tends to carry itself well: open chest, a walk that takes up its proper share of the footpath, often hair or clothes with some flourish to them. You start things wholeheartedly or not at all, and you're poor at slipping in unnoticed even when you'd like to. Strangers give you attention you didn't ask for, and they often assume you're more confident than you feel. Your instinct under pressure is to slow down and get warmer, where most people speed up and get sharper.

People decide quickly that you can be trusted with something, and they're usually right. You can walk into a tense room, a nervous class, a family argument, and your ease gives everyone a lower gear to drop into. Because the Sun rules your chart, your whole life tends to go better when you let yourself be visible; hiding costs you more energy than showing up does. You're also good with actual wariness: the snappy dog, the defensive teenager, the prickly new client. You don't crowd them, you don't back off, and sooner or later they come over.

A calm exterior this convincing can become a job. You may feel you aren't allowed an off day, because everyone has cast you as the unshakeable one and you've half agreed. Then the gap between the face and the inside widens, and nobody thinks to ask how you are. Leo rising also bruises easily when ignored: being overlooked at the door, talked across, left off the list, can sting far more than it should, and you'd hate anyone to see it. Warmth that has to be noticed starts turning into performance, and you can feel the difference even if no one else can.

People are often drawn to the glow first and meet the person second, so part of your work in love is slowing that down. Let someone see you unlit: tired, unsure, not hosting. With Leo on the first house, Aquarius, the facing sign, falls on your house of partners, and you're often pulled to cooler, more independent people who won't simply orbit you. That's healthy friction. They give you room; you give them heat. The trouble starts only if you read their need for space as a verdict on you. It rarely is.

You get handed the front-of-house role whether or not you applied for it: the presentation, the difficult customer, the welcome speech. You're good at it, and first impressions do real work for you in interviews and pitches. Use that honestly. The thing to guard against is being hired for your presence and then coasting on it, or letting colleagues assume you're fine with pressure because you look fine. Say when the load is too much. And build in unobserved time to prepare. The ease people admire is real, but it holds up best when there's homework under it.

Before you walk into any room that matters this week, stop at the door for one breath. Drop your shoulders, unclench your jaw, and ask yourself a single question: am I about to perform warm, or be warm? If it's the first, find one person in the room to be plainly curious about and start there. Then, once this week, answer 'how are you' truthfully to someone safe. You're teaching your face and your inside to match, which is the whole difference between the woman on the card and a person merely acting brave.

asBirthCard.p: This card comes from your birthdate, not from any sign in your chart. Add every digit of the date and keep adding until you land on a number from 1 to 22; yours lands on eight, and Strength is the eighth Major in the Rider-Waite deck. Eight is four doubled: structure that has been tested and built again. Turn the numeral on its side and you get the lemniscate floating over the woman's head, a loop with no end. So eight speaks of power that renews through rhythm and repetition. It marks a life shaped by stamina more than conquest.

As a lifelong pattern, eight shows up as the same kind of test arriving in different clothes. Every few years there's a situation with teeth: a difficult boss, a volatile relative, a fear of your own, an appetite that wants to run the house. Each time the blunt approach fails and the patient one works, and each time you seem to have to learn that afresh. You may notice you're at your best in the long middle of things, after the excitement and before the finish, where other people lose heart. Endurance is your native speed.

What you get from this is a strength that compounds. Someone who has calmed the lion a dozen times stops being frightened of lions. By midlife an eight person usually has an unusual tolerance for intensity, their own and other people's, and a reputation for being good in a crisis without being dramatic about it. You're hard to provoke and hard to wear down. There's a quieter gift too: you understand from the inside that wild things, including wild people, respond to respect. That makes you a natural with whatever others have written off as too difficult.

The eight loop can also run the wrong way. Being good at enduring, you may endure what you ought to leave: the draining job, the one-sided friendship, the situation you keep gentling that never gentles. Patience turns into a way of avoiding the harder act of saying no. The other side of the shadow is control. Having learnt to manage your own lion, you can start managing everyone's, reading each room for risk and never quite relaxing. And when you do slip, lose your temper, give in to the appetite, you judge yourself far more harshly than the slip deserves.

In relationships you're the one who stays steady when things get loud, and partners often lean on that. It's a real strength. Check, though, whether you keep choosing people who need calming: the pattern can cast you as the permanent handler, with love feeling like work you happen to be good at. You deserve someone who sometimes puts a hand on your lion too. Let yourself be the unreasonable one now and then, the one who's scared or furious or needs looking after. A bond where only one person is ever composed isn't balanced, however peaceful it looks.

You're suited to anything that rewards long patience with something living or volatile: teaching, caring work, training animals, managing people, negotiation, rehabilitation, slow craft. You're the person given the account nobody else could keep, and you keep it. Eight is also the number of steady repetition, so skills come to you through practice rather than flashes, and you shouldn't measure yourself against quick starters. Your risk at work is absorbing too much. Because you can take pressure, more gets sent your way. Learn to notice the load while it's still a choice, and to name a limit without apologising for it.

Pick the one recurring thing that's testing you at the moment, a person, a habit, a fear, and for one week meet it at the same time each day for five minutes only. Five minutes of the hard conversation's first draft, five minutes sitting with the craving before deciding, five minutes of the dreaded task. Then stop, even if it's going well. Eight works by rhythm: small, regular, unforced contact. At the end of the week, write one line on what has shifted, and whether the thing looks any smaller for having been met daily.
